info.title: Copybara for .NET
info.description: A tool for transforming and moving code between repositories (.NET port of Google Copybara). Installs the `copybara` command; workflows are declared in Starlark in a copy.bara.sky file.

options.name: --allow-empty-diff
options.description: If set to false, Copybara will not write to the destination if the exact same change is already pending in the destination. Currently only supported for `git.github_pr_destination` and `git.gerrit_destination`.

options.name: --baseline-for-merge-import
options.description: Origin baseline to use for merge import. This overrides any inferred origin baseline

options.name: --change-request-from-sot-limit
options.description: Number of origin baseline changes to use for trying to match one in the destination. It can be used if the are many parent changes in the origin that are a no-op in the destination

options.name: --change-request-from-sot-retry
options.description: Number of retries and delay between retries when we cannot find the baseline in the destination for CHANGE_REQUEST_FROM_SOT. For example '10,30,60' will retry three times. The first retry will be delayed 10s, the second one 30s and the third one 60s

options.name: --change-request-parent
options.description: Commit revision to be used as parent when importing a commit using CHANGE_REQUEST workflow mode. This shouldn't be needed in general as Copybara is able to detect the parent commit message.

options.name: --check-last-rev-state
options.description: If enabled, Copybara will validate that the destination didn't change since last-rev import for destination_files. Note that this flag doesn't work for CHANGE_REQUEST mode.

options.name: --commands-timeout
options.description: Commands timeout

options.name: --config-root
options.description: Configuration root path to be used for resolving absolute config labels like '//foo/bar'

options.name: --console-file-flush-interval
options.description: How often Copybara should flush the console to the output file. (10s, 1m, etc.)If set to 0s, console will be flushed only at the end.

options.name: --console-file-path
options.description: If set, write the console output also to the given file path.

options.name: --default-author
options.description: Use this author as default instead of the one in the config file.Format should be 'Foo Bar <foobar@example.com>'

options.name: --diff-bin
options.description: Command line diff tool bin used in merge import. Defaults to diff3, but users can pass in their own diffing tools (along with requisite arg reordering)

options.name: --diff-in-origin
options.description: When this flag is enabled, copybara will show different changes between last Revision and current revision in origin instead of in destination. NOTE: it Only works for SQUASH and ITERATIVE

options.name: --disable-consistency-merge-import
options.description: If merge import is set to use consistency in the config, disable it for this run. This uses an import baseline instead. A new consistency file will still be generated.

options.name: --disable-reversible-check
options.description: If set, all workflows will be executed without reversible_check, overriding the  workflow config and the normal behavior for CHANGE_REQUEST mode.

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: Run the migration in dry-run mode. Some destination implementations might have some side effects (like creating a code review), but never submit to a main branch.

options.name: --event-monitor
options.description: Eventmonitors to enable. These must be in the list of available monitors.

options.name: --force-update
options.description: Force the migration even if Copybara cannot find in the destination a change that is an ancestor of the one(s) being migrated. This should be used with care, as it could lose changes when migrating a previous/conflicting change.

options.name: --force-author
options.description: Force the author to this. Note that this only changes the author before the transformations happen, you can still use the transformations to alter it.

options.name: --force-message
options.description: Force the change description to this. Note that this only changes the message before the transformations happen, you can still use the transformations to alter it.

options.name: --ignore-noop
options.description: Only warn about operations/transforms that didn't have any effect. For example: A transform that didn't modify any file, non-existent origin directories, etc.

options.name: --import-noop-changes
options.description: By default Copybara will only try to migrate changes that could affect the destination. Ignoring changes that only affect excluded files in origin_files. This flag disables that behavior and runs for all the changes.

options.name: --info-include-definition
options.description: When set, the INFO command will include the migrations' definition stack info in the table or list output. In table, leaves out origin, destination and mode.

options.name: --info-include-versions
options.description: Include upstream versions in the info command output.

options.name: --info-list-only
options.description: When set, the INFO command will print a list of workflows defined in the file.

options.name: --init-history
options.description: Import all the changes from the beginning of the history up to the resolved ref. For 'ITERATIVE' workflows this will import individual changes since the first one. For 'SQUASH' it will import the squashed change up to the resolved ref. WARNING: Use with care, this flag should be used only for the very first run of Copybara for a workflow.

options.name: --iterative-limit-changes
options.description: Import just a number of changes instead of all the pending ones

options.name: --labels
options.description: Additional flags. Can be accessed in feedback and mirror context objects via the `cli_labels` field. In `core.workflow`, they are accessible as labels, but with names uppercased and prefixed with FLAG_ to avoid name clashes with existing labels. I.e. `--labels=label1:value1` will define a label FLAG_LABEL1Format: --labels=flag1:value1,flag2:value2 Or: --labels flag1:value1,flag2:value2

options.name: --last-rev
options.description: Last revision that was migrated to the destination

options.name: --noansi
options.description: Don't use ANSI output for messages

options.name: --nocleanup
options.description: Cleanup the output directories. This includes the workdir, scratch clones of Git repos, etc. By default is set to false and directories will be cleaned prior to the execution. If set to true, the previous run output will not be cleaned up. Keep in mind that running in this mode will lead to an ever increasing disk usage.

options.name: --noprompt
options.description: Don't prompt, this will answer all prompts with 'yes'

options.name: --nosmart-prune
options.description: Disable smart prunning

options.name: --notransformation-join
options.description: By default Copybara tries to join certain transformations in one so that it is more efficient. This disables the feature.

options.name: --output-limit
options.description: Limit the output in the console to a number of records. Each subcommand might use this flag differently. Defaults to 0, which shows all the output.

options.name: --output-root
options.description: The root directory where to generate output files. If not set, ~/copybara/out is used by default. Use with care, Copybara might remove files inside this root if necessary.

options.name: --patch-bin
options.description: Path for GNU Patch command

options.name: --read-config-from-change
options.description: For each imported origin change, load the workflow's origin_files, destination_files and transformations from the config version of that change. The rest of the fields (more importantly, origin and destination) cannot change and the version from the first config will be used.

options.name: --read-config-from-change-disable
options.description: --read-config-from-change is a arity 0 flag, this flag overrides it to override it being enabled.

options.name: --repo-timeout
options.description: Repository operation timeout duration.

options.name: --same-version
options.description: Re-import the last version imported. This is useful for example to check that a refactor in a copy.bara.sky file doesn't introduce accidental changes.

options.name: --skip-transforms
options.description: List of transform names that should be skipped.

options.name: --squash
options.description: Override workflow's mode with 'SQUASH'. This is useful mainly for workflows that use 'ITERATIVE' mode, when we want to run a single export with 'SQUASH', maybe to fix an issue. Always use --dry-run before, to test your changes locally.

options.name: --squash-skip-history
options.description: Avoid exposing the history of changes that are being migrated. This is useful when we want to migrate a new repository but we don't want to expose all the change history to metadata.squash_notes.

options.name: --threads
options.description: Number of threads to use when running transformations that change lot of files

options.name: --threads-for-merge-import
options.description: Number of threads to use for executing the diff tool for the merge import mode.

options.name: --threads-min-size
options.description: Minimum size of the lists to process to run them in parallel

options.name: --to-folder
options.description: Sometimes a user wants to test what the outcome would be for a workflow without changing the configuration or adding an auxiliary testing workflow. This flag allows to change an existing workflow to use folder.destination

options.name: --validate-starlark
options.description: Starlark should be validated prior to execution, but this might break legacy configs. Options are LOOSE, STRICT

options.name: --version-selector-use-cli-ref
options.description: If command line ref is to used with a version selector, pass this flag to tell copybara to use it.

options.name: --work-dir
options.description: Directory where all the transformations will be performed. By default a temporary directory.

options.name: --workflow-identity-user
options.description: Use a custom string as a user for computing change identity

options.name: --verbose
options.description:
Verbose output.
Additional flags. Can be accessed in feedback and mirror context objects via the `cli_labels` field. In `core.workflow`, they are accessible as labels, but with names uppercased and prefixed with FLAG_ to avoid name clashes with existing labels. I.e. `--labels=label1:value1` will define a label FLAG_LABEL1Format: --labels=flag1:value1,flag2:value2 Or: --labels flag1:value1,flag2:value2
